Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

carry verb

also carry around, bear, lug

classical

Ov. F. 4.509–510: domum glandēs … portat
Hor. S. 1.5.90: umerīs portāre

portō, portāre, portāvī, portātum

verb, first conjugation

carry (a load)

Of carrying something, often heavy, from one place to another (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — carry, bear; bring

    verb, irregular · also used · classical · Liv. 2.32.10: nē manūs ad ōs cibum ferrent

    The general verb, also “bring” and “bear”.

  • gestō, gestāre, gestāvī, gestātum — carry about; carry (a child) in one’s arms

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 563: in manibus gestāvī meīs

    (vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum (Lewis & Short); in cōmoediā Plaut., Ter.)

    The verb for carrying a small child about: in manibus gestāre.

  • bājulō, bājulāre — carry a heavy load, luggage

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 4.1.5: asinum … bājulantem sarcinās; Traupman 215, 287: carry (luggage)

    (vōx ante et post aetātem classicam: Plaut., Phaedr. (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • ille domum glandēs excussaque mōra rubētīs portat et ārsūrīs ārida ligna focīs

    he was carrying home acorns and blackberries shaken from the brambles, and dry wood for the fireOv. F. 4.509–510

  • quem ego modo puerum tantillum in manibus gestāvī meīs

    whom only the other day I carried in my arms, a tiny little boyTer. Ad. 563

  • vēnālēs umerō fascēs portābat in urbem

    he used to carry bundles to town on his shoulder, to sellMor. 81

  • Alter alterīus onera portāte

    Carry one another’s burdensVulg. Gal. 6.2

See also bring, hold in one’s arms, carry on one’s shoulders, lift.
